annotations.annotation_text: Swiftian presence "swift" on page 486 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): the Dean of St. Patrick's Cathedral haunts this passage within the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. His dual lovers Stella and Vanessa mirror Issy's split personalities, while his savage satire infuses the Age of Men dream with political and scatological ferocity.
sources: Ehrenpreis, Irvin. Swift: The Man, His Works, and the Age. https://archive.org/details/swiftmanhisworks01ehre

annotations.annotation_text: Book of Kells motif "initial" on page 486 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): Joyce equates the Wake's labyrinthine text with the 8th-century illuminated Gospel at Trinity College Dublin within the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. During this Age of Men phase, the monastic scribe and the barnyard Hen both decode divine messages from material surfaces.
sources: Trinity College Dublin: The Book of Kells Online. https://digitalcollections.tcd.ie/concern/works/hm50tr726
